newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka police arrest six in MP killing.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka police arrest six in MP killing.

text.p: Sri Lanka police arrested six people in connection with the killing of a ruling coalition legislator whose death sparked riots in southern Sri Lanka this week, a police spokesman said on Friday.

The spokesman for Colombo police headquarters declined to name the six but police sources said they did not include two named suspects, legislator Susantha Punchinilame of the opposition United National Party (UNP) and Mahinda Ratnatilleke, the former UNP mayor of Ratnapura city,
Police on Thursday offered one million rupees ($17,500) to anyone with information leading to the arrest of the two named suspects.
Police sources in Ratnapura said the names of the six people arrested could not be released until they were arraigned before the local magistrate.

Gunmen shot and killed Nalanda Ellawala, 29, a member of parliament from the ruling People's Alliance, on Tuesday during a roadside quarrel in Ratnapura, 80 km (50 miles) southwest of Colombo, between his supporters and rivals from the UNP.

Pro-People's Alliance supporters in Ratnapura set fire to scores of buildings owned by UNP supporters on Tuesday and Wednesday, but the area was under control by Thursday, police said. No one was hurt in the riots.
People's Alliance legislators said hundreds of thousands of people were expected to attend Ellawala's funeral on Saturday and warned of more violence.

The killing occurred the day before a deadline for filing nominations for local elections on March 21, the first electoral contest between President Chandrika Kumaratunga's People's Alliance and the UNP since 1994, when Kumaratunga's group ousted the UNP from 17 years in power.
